subject: Demo recap — quality guardrails, model recommendations, and sample prompts
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Hayes <oliver.hayes@lumosai.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Demo recap — quality guardrails, model recommendations, and sample prompts

Thanks again for the demo this morning — really appreciate you walking us through LumosAI's end-user flows. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

Summary (what we heard)
- Primary use: intent classification + short-form response generation inside your support console.
- Volume: ~18M monthly messages, peak bursts during releases.
- Constraints: sub-150ms user-facing latency target for autocomplete-style responses; strict PII redaction across EU and US data.

Immediate next steps (what we need from you)
1) Sample prompts & edge cases: please share ~200 representative prompts across the top 10 intent taxonomies and flag ~10 that you consider "sensitive" (PII, legal, financial). We will use these for model fit and regression checks.
2) Redaction guidance: if you can highlight which fields are always redacted vs. those that can be pseudonymized, that will speed our intake.
3) Benchmarks & priorities: we shared a short benchmark summary during the call — Ben will follow up with recommended candidate models and a short SLO mapping for latency vs. cost.

I've attached a short intake sheet to make prompt upload easy (shared-prompt-intake-sheet.xlsx). If you prefer, you can drop the CSV into the Drive link below and give us edit access.

Proposed timeline
- You upload prompts by Tue 8/31.
- We run initial fit and return a 1-page model recommendation + benchmark snapshot by Fri 9/3.
- Quick sync (30m) the week of 9/6 to walk results and guardrail options.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aBzPromptIntake
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/4521

Attachments: [shared-prompt-intake-sheet.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

Thanks — looking forward to the samples.

— Lauren

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Demo recap — quality guardrails, model recommendations, and sample prompts

Hi Oliver / Samira — thanks for the quick reply and for starting with the 150-row export. Short answers up front: Redwood can accept already-redacted data, but we can also run a light ingestion-time redaction pipeline if you'd like (we'll log the transformations and provide a redaction report). If you prefer us to handle redaction, we just need a sample schema and an explicit list of fields to remove/pseudonymize.

Model recommendations (initial candidate set)
- rw-instruct-medium-13b-q4 (balanced quality/cost) — recommended for early A/B against your existing rules-based generator
- redwood-vicuna-13b-q4f16 (low-latency, strong on short-instruction responses)
- rw-llama2-70b-8k (higher-quality fallback for ambiguous/longer replies; keep for non-interactive background-generation)

Benchmarks & guardrails
- Attached: redwood-model-benchmarks-2026.pdf — contains latency/QPS numbers at your estimated avg seq length (we measured 32 tokens output / 18 token input).
- Quality regression concerns: please flag any production prompts that are "must not degrade" (e.g., legal reply templates). We'll hold those in an evaluation set and run nightly regression checks during rollout.
- Guardrail options: token-level safety filters, response length caps, semantic similarity checks to canonical responses, and model-fallback policies when confidence < 0.4. We'll outline an automated escalation flow if a request hits multiple safety signals.

Prompt sampling guidance (what we need from you)
- ~200 prompts covering core intents; include at least 20 examples of edge cases (ambiguous intent, nested intents, multi-turn context).
- Mark columns: intent, user_text, expected_response (optional), sensitivity_flag (yes/no).
- For PHI/PII: if you'd like Redwood to handle redaction, send one representative PII-containing sample row and the schema; we will redact in a deterministic way and return the redacted artifact for approval.

Logging, security, and procurement
- We'll link this thread to the HubSpot deal (RW-DEAL-4521).
- If you want the private onboarding track (SOC2 evidence + isolated tenancy), say so and we will route to Solutions Engineering for scoping.

Timelines
- With your sample upload by 8/31, we can deliver an initial model-fit report + benchmark snapshot by 9/3.

Drive (upload): https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aBzPromptIntake
Benchmarks (internal): https://redwood-internal.example.com/benchmarks/2026
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/4521

Attachments: [redwood-model-benchmarks-2026.pdf (application/pdf)]

If helpful, Marissa can coordinate the initial evaluation job once the CSV is in Drive — looping her here.

— Ben
